literal: The elder, to Gaius the beloved, whom I love in truth.
prose: The elder, to the beloved Gaius, whom I love in truth.

literal: Beloved, concerning all things I pray you to prosper and to be in health, just as your soul prospers.
prose: Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers.

literal: I rejoiced for greatly, brothers coming and testifying to your truth, just as you in truth walk.
prose: For I rejoiced greatly when brothers came and testified to your truth, just as you walk in truth.

literal: Greater than these things I do not have joy, that I hear my children walking in the truth.
prose: I have no greater joy than this, than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.

literal: Beloved, [you] do a faithful thing, whatever you work for the brothers, and this [for] strangers,
prose: Beloved, you act faithfully in whatever you do for the brothers, even though they are strangers,

literal: who testified to your love before [the] church, whom you will do well, having sent forward worthily of God.
prose: who testified to your love before the church; you will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.

literal: For on behalf of the Name they went out, taking nothing from the Gentiles.
prose: For they went out for the sake of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.

literal: We therefore ought to support such [men], in order that we may become fellow-workers with the truth.
prose: We, then, ought to support such people, so that we may become fellow workers with the truth.

literal: I-wrote something to-the church; but the [one] loving-to-be-first of-them, Diotrephes, not receives us.
prose: I wrote something to the church; but Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them, does not welcome us.

literal: Because of this, if I come, I will remind [him] of the works that he is doing, prating against us with wicked words; and not being content with these things, neither does he himself receive the brothers, and those wishing [to] he hinders, and out of the church casts [them] out.
prose: Therefore, if I come, I will remind him of the works he is doing, gossiping against us with wicked words; and not content with that, he himself does not receive the brothers, and he hinders those who want to, and throws them out of the church.

literal: Beloved, do not imitate the evil, but the good. The [one] doing-good is of God; the [one] doing-evil has-not seen God.
prose: Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. The one who does good is of God; the one who does evil has not seen God.

literal: To Demetrius it has been testified by all, and by the truth itself; and we, but, testify, and you know that the testimony of us true is.
prose: Demetrius has been testified to by everyone, and by the truth itself; and we also testify, and you know that our testimony is true.

literal: Many things I had to write to you, but not I want through ink and reed [pen] to you to write;
prose: I had many things to write to you, but I do not want to write to you with ink and pen;

literal: I hope but to see you at once, and mouth to mouth we will speak.
prose: But I hope to see you at once, and we will speak face to face.

literal: Peace [be] to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends according to name.
prose: Peace to you. The friends greet you. Greet the friends by name.
